title: Trade acknowledgement strength for failure availability
description: Use a single-datacenter RF=3 replica set. Change the read and write consistency levels, then remove replicas to see which operations can complete and whether successful quorums must overlap.

levels.label: ONE
levels.detail: The coordinator needs one replica response.

levels.label: QUORUM
levels.detail: A majority of the three replicas must respond.

levels.label: ALL
levels.detail: Every replica in this datacenter must respond.

scenarios.label: All replicas reachable
scenarios.detail: Three replicas can receive and answer the operation.
scenarios.consequence: Every modeled consistency level can complete, subject to real latency and timeout limits.
scenarios.repairNote: No replica is intentionally missing this mutation, but scheduled repair still detects divergence from other causes.

scenarios.label: One replica unavailable
scenarios.detail: Two replicas answer while one misses the normal request path.
scenarios.consequence: ONE and QUORUM can complete; ALL cannot. A successful response at a lower level does not mean every copy is current.
scenarios.repairNote: Hints may replay the missed write when the replica returns, but hints are best effort. Repair remains the convergence mechanism.

scenarios.label: Two replicas unavailable
scenarios.detail: Only one of the three replicas can answer.
scenarios.consequence: Only ONE can complete. QUORUM and ALL sacrifice availability rather than acknowledge with too few responses.
scenarios.repairNote: When failed replicas return, operators must keep the repair schedule inside the table's tombstone safety window.
